issues.subject: Notes from the darkroom: the dusk rolls
issues.text:
Contact Sheet · {date}

Notes from the darkroom: the dusk rolls

Late October is when I find out which camera will let me change a roll in gloves. This one's going out on 21 October, with the same old camera and a new batch of sleeves.

Elliot Moor's last light
Elliot made this set along the New Cut between the last dog walk and the first lit windows. The frames he'd marked as too thin were my favourites once we put them under the enlarger. In the last pair, the pavement is the brightest thing in the picture and the water has almost gone. We've asked him to put both frames up for the open table on 24 October.
https://contactsheet.example/work/elliot-moor-last-light

The clipped corner at the lab
North Lock Lab changed to sleeves cut for strips of six this month. They can still do strips of four if you write it on the order envelope, which matters for those of us with the smaller binders. They're putting one clipped corner on the sheet so you can tell which way round it was fed into the scanner. The lab note shows the two sleeve layouts with a ruler beside them.
https://contactsheet.example/lab/north-lock-sleeve-change

A grey card in the evening
Hana brought in the first and last frames of a roll exposed ten minutes apart, then printed the middles on the same strip. You could watch the trees disappear one stop at a time. She uses a bit of card in the first frame so she can get back to roughly the same grade when she prints again. Her notebook has the times as well as the exposures.
https://contactsheet.example/notes/grey-card-at-dusk

Good luck in the dark,
Edie Rolfe, editor

issues.subject: Three prints from a bent negative
issues.text:
Contact Sheet · {date}

Three prints from a bent negative

A negative from the July pile wouldn't lie flat, even after three nights under a dictionary. Jo made good on his offer to show me how he tapes one down.

Jo Bell's window portraits
Jo made them at the window of a watch repair shop about to close. In the second picture you can see the contact cement around the edge of the counter, and in the third there's a faint reflection of the other watch repair shop across the road. We scanned his contact sheet with the grease pencil still visible so you can see he made quite a different selection the first time.
https://contactsheet.example/work/jo-bell-window-portraits

At the enlarger: the glass carrier
The glass carrier at the east bench had a fine haze on its upper plate. That's gone and the corner clip has been replaced. A negative that bows out of the metal holder sits much better in it now, but clean both sides before you close it. There's a photograph in the bench notes of the dust by the frame edge that we missed on the first pass.
https://contactsheet.example/lab/east-bench-glass-carrier

Swap evening for sheet film holders
If you've got an orphaned four-by-five holder, put an elastic round it with a scrap of card saying what you know about it. Bring it along to the open table and write your name inside the elastic if you want it back. We had a box of six by the tea urn last time and three were still loaded. There will be a changing bag this time as well.
https://contactsheet.example/notices/holder-swap

Good luck in the dark,
Edie Rolfe, editor

issues.subject: One lens for the river
issues.text:
Contact Sheet · {date}

One lens for the river

I went out with the fifty and spent half the walk wishing it were wider. There were two good pictures at the end. One of them was of a bench I'd walked past to get the view.

The ferry landing from one spot
May Winter copied the same shot every six mornings for two months from a mark in the mud next to the slipway. Three frames have just enough difference in the idle ropes to be worth setting side by side. She's left the sprocket holes showing where each frame starts. At the reading table we found ourselves trying to guess which part of the river was advancing because there were no reflections to go on.
https://contactsheet.example/work/may-winter-ferry-landing

Why the test strip starts wider
The old strip cutter in the small darkroom made pieces that were too narrow to get the sky and the side of the building into the same test. Mina's set a spare guide on the guillotine. The tray beside it now holds two-inch strips to share. The example in the bench notes uses three two-second steps. Adjust from there once you've seen what your own paper does under the lamp.
https://contactsheet.example/lab/test-strip-on-fibre

Negative sleeves by post
Most of this month's order went to the regular table, but I have 120 sleeves left for 120 roll film. There's a box marked with the size by the door, or I can put ten in a stiff envelope. Tell me if your binder takes four holes. The first bundle I pulled off the shelf was punched for three, and I'd rather spend the time checking here than waste your return postage.
https://contactsheet.example/notices/august-sleeve-batch

Good luck in the dark,
Edie Rolfe, editor

Contact Sheet · 5 Silverbirch Yard, London SE8 3BX
